audit.scope: Cargo.lock dependency policy; not mathematical correctness

deny.scope: Cargo.lock dependency policy; not mathematical correctness

correctness_status: Independent finite reference proof and changed-operation validation are separate requirements. Dependency policy success does not prove correct rounding.
cpu_policy: No CPU requirement changed. Generic x64 uses runtime FMA detection; actual non-FMA qualification remains pending.

rerun.deny: advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok (exit 0, identical to deny.log)
rerun.audit: no vulnerabilities in 80 locked crates (exit 0, identical to audit.log)

packages.autocfg 1.5.1: Apache-2.0 OR MIT (MIT used; build-time only)

license.compatibility: MIT is a permissive license compatible with distribution under GPL-2.0-only; Apache-2.0 alone is not, so the MIT alternative is the one relied on for dual-licensed packages. deny.toml allows MIT and rejects other licenses for these packages.
license.optional_dependency: metallic declares an optional `rug` (GMP, LGPL) dependency for its own tests/tools; martensite-cmath uses default features, `rug` is absent from Cargo.lock and is never built.

pinning.lockfile: all four packages pinned by version and crates.io checksum (packages list above)
pinning.change_policy: Changing the pin changes recorded results and is a reviewed behavior change (#201).

trust.metallic_unsafe: 58 `unsafe` occurrences in src: target_feature FMA dispatch after runtime CPU detection and similar intrinsics; accounted for as an established dependency, not as workspace unsafe code.
trust.build_script: build.rs only emits a cargo warning when x86 targets lack compile-time FMA; it reads no files and runs no programs.
trust.correct_rounding_claim: Upstream states every f32/f64 function is correctly rounded (ties to even), checked against CORE-MATH and MPFR. For the kernel, every differing call reached by the workspace tests was checked against MPFR in ../attribution/.
trust.cpu: x86-64 builds use runtime FMA detection; on CPUs without FMA some polynomial paths fall back to unfused multiply-add. The release matrix compares exact result words on its four runners; CPUs without FMA are not qualified, and no minimum CPU requirement was raised.

decision: Accepted: license compatible with GPL-2.0-only, versions pinned exactly, cargo deny and cargo audit clean. The finite-CPU qualification limit above remains recorded.
